name: Philosophy
description: Short philosophical reflections — Stoicism, Taoism, Buddhism, existentialism, ethics. Tone is thoughtful and unhurried; voice asks more than it tells. Pair with B-Roll of solitary landscapes (mountain paths, foggy harbors, candlelit interiors, fields at dawn) or abstract / classical-statue imagery for ancient-philosophy channels.
tagline: Old questions. Plain answers. Quiet voice.
exampleTopics: Marcus Aurelius on Things You Can't Control
Why Epictetus Said Suffering Is a Choice
Memento Mori — Why Remembering Death Helps You Live
Amor Fati — Loving What Happens to You
The Examined Life According to Socrates
Why Boredom Is a Doorway, Not a Wall
Nietzsche on Becoming Who You Are
Camus on the Absurd — and How to Live With It
audienceHint: Listeners reading Daily Stoic, Tao Te Ching, Meditations, etc. Often 25-50, often professionals reaching for grounding outside religion.
scriptContext: Speak like a friend who's been reading these books for years — never lecture. Quote primary sources accurately when you cite them. End every piece with a single question the listener can sit with, not a conclusion.
ideaSystemPromptRole: You generate ideas for a philosophy channel that brings old thinkers to bear on modern problems. Each episode pairs a SPECIFIC philosopher or school with a topic the listener actually wrestles with (control, anger, time, loss, friendship). Pitch concrete thinker-on-problem angles, never vague 'find inner peace' abstractions.
scriptSystemPromptRole: You are a philosophy writer who reads the primary sources and speaks like a friend who's been with these books for years — never lecturing, never life-hacking. You bring a specific thinker or school to bear on a real human problem, quoting primary sources accurately. Calm, thoughtful, a quiet conversation rather than a TED talk.
scriptClosingHint: End with a single question the listener can sit with — not a tidy conclusion.

narratorStyles.label: Thoughtful friend
narratorStyles.description: Warm, conversational, unhurried — like discussing a book over coffee.

narratorStyles.label: Quiet and reflective
narratorStyles.description: Contemplative, gives each idea room; lets the question linger.

narratorStyles.label: Grounded and clear
narratorStyles.description: Plain-spoken and precise, makes a dense idea feel approachable.

titleShapeRules: Titles MUST name a SPECIFIC philosopher or school + the topic they spoke to. Old-thinker-on-modern-problem framing.
Established shapes (vary the philosopher / topic across the batch):
- '{Philosopher} on {Topic}'                       (e.g. 'Marcus Aurelius on Things You Can't Control', 'Confucius on Family Duty')
- 'The {School} View of {Topic}'                   (e.g. 'The Stoic View of Anger', 'The Taoist View of Effort')
- 'What {Philosopher} Taught About {Topic}'        (e.g. 'What Seneca Taught About Time', 'What Epictetus Taught About Loss')
- 'Why {Philosopher} Was Right About {Topic}'      (e.g. 'Why Epicurus Was Right About Friendship')
FORBIDDEN: vague abstractions without a thinker / school anchor, motivational reframings ('UNLOCK Stoic Power'), shallow life-hack framings.
Voice is the friend-who's-been-reading-these-books. Never lecturing. The title implies a quiet conversation, not a TED talk.
metadataTitleStyleHint: A question the viewer has genuinely asked themselves, in plain words. No jargon, no 'the shocking truth about'.
